value.title: Marginal-balance and correlation pruning for two-letter Marton gain
value.statement: For the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, consider any finite-auxiliary Marton law (W,U,V)-X_1X_2-(Y^2,Z^2) with unnormalized two-letter Marton sum value M. Let q_i=Pr[X_i=1], Q=q_1+q_2, C_out=I(Y_1;Y_2)+I(Z_1;Z_2), c_in=Pr[X_1X_2=11]-q_1q_2, and T=2L_RTD. If M>T, then q_1,q_2∈(3/8,5/8), and therefore q_1,q_2∈(7/20,13/20); moreover 17/20<Q<23/20, C_out<7/160=0.04375<0.044 bits, and |c_in|<7/40. On the reflected/transposed family Pr[00]=Pr[11]=alpha and Pr[01]=Pr[10]=1/2-alpha, M>T additionally requires 1/8<alpha<5/13. These are necessary conditions only: they neither construct nor prove a two-letter gain, rule one out, nor provide a capacity converse.
scopeQualifications: Applies only to the governed half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}.
Applies to finite-auxiliary laws and the unnormalized two-letter Marton sum value.
Every conclusion is a necessary condition conditional on M>T=2L_RTD.
Only the unconditional RTD calculus and directed threshold certificate are used from the threshold foundation; neither (H-Marton) nor (H-binary) is used.
The alpha-window applies only to the stated reflected/transposed one-parameter input family.
The result does not construct or prove a two-letter gain.
The result does not rule out a two-letter gain.
The result is not a capacity converse.

proofs: Memorylessness gives the exact decomposition G(P_{X_1X_2})=F(q_1)+F(q_2)-C_out/2 for the averaged product-channel input mutual information.
Combining that identity and the two pre-averaging Marton-to-input rows with strictly concave coordinatewise envelopes forces q_1,q_2∈(3/8,5/8) and 17/20<Q<23/20 whenever M>T.
Reflection symmetry and the maximum of the one-coordinate average curve give C_out<7/160<0.044 bits.
The channel's affine output laws identify each receiver-pair covariance as c_in/4; Pinsker's inequality then converts the output mutual-information bound into |c_in|<7/40.
For the reflected/transposed one-parameter family, monotonicity of the exact output-correlation expression and certified endpoint comparisons force 1/8<alpha<5/13.
methods: Directed interval arithmetic and rational cutoff certification
Monotonicity analysis on the reflected/transposed family
computations: The submitted directed checker reconstructs the exact RTD threshold, verifies the coordinate and sum-envelope separations, brackets the sharp crossings, certifies C_out<7/160<0.044 and the rational covariance comparison, and verifies the two symmetric-family endpoint inequalities.
tools: The submitted Python standard-library checker uses exact rational arithmetic and outward-rounded 120-digit Decimal intervals without network access or external packages.

value.title: Multiletter Marton support search
value.objective: Determine whether multiletter Marton coding can strictly improve the current half-skew BSSC achievable rate, and rigorously characterize the super-input support and auxiliary structure required by any such improvement.
value.currentStateSummary: The finite-auxiliary multiletter Marton sequence is unconditionally bounded and superadditive, has the Fekete normalized limit, and scales exactly under independent repetition of a selected law. The exact randomized-time-division value L_RTD and directed strict intervals for L_RTD and 2L_RTD are certified; capacity lower bounds and identification of the one-letter Marton optimum require the separate stated hypotheses, and no fixed-blocklength equality is a capacity converse. Conditional-product Marton laws are additive on finite receiver-skew channels, while every arbitrary finite two-letter gaining law must pass all four constant-padding correlation tests. Every two-letter law supported on at most three super-input symbols has value below 0.695 bits, so a witness exceeding twice the optimal one-letter RTD value must have full support with masses above 1/180 on 00 and 11 and above 1/325 on 01 and 10. Further necessary pruning now shows that M>2L_RTD forces each input marginal into (3/8,5/8), the marginal sum into (17/20,23/20), total within-receiver output correlation below 7/160 bits, and input covariance magnitude below 7/40; on the reflected/transposed one-parameter family it also forces 1/8<alpha<5/13. These conditions are necessary only and neither establish nor exclude a gain. Whether any full-support, genuinely conditionally coupled law satisfying all filters can gain remains open.
value.localResidualSummary: Restrict the two-letter search to genuinely nonfactorizable full-support finite Marton laws satisfying the certified symbol-mass floors, all four padding-correlation tests, q_1,q_2∈(3/8,5/8), 17/20<q_1+q_2<23/20, C_out<7/160, and |c_in|<7/40; retain the crossed padding tests separately. Within the reflected/transposed family, restrict to 1/8<alpha<5/13. Seek either stronger interior pruning or a certified law above 2L_RTD. Independently authenticate or prove (H-Marton) and (H-binary), investigate finite-auxiliary cardinality control and extensions beyond finite auxiliaries, and keep superadditivity distinct from additivity and fixed-blocklength optimization distinct from a capacity converse.

value.title: Canonical problem
value.currentStateSummary: Four complementary directions are established. Genuine deterministic finite-block private-message codes induce approximate dependence balance, a fixed encoder-coordinate map, and four compatible rate rows, while an explicit nonbinary witness obstructs the specified coarse entropy and finite copy-lemma route; fixed-cardinality auxiliaries and exact BSSC posterior consistency remain unresolved. The separately relaxed UV scalars tensorize, with receiver-skew symmetry giving equality of the branchwise and averaged scalars and half-skew BSSC product values n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4), but these scalars do not establish capacity. Conditional on the exact encoded Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 premise, the private-message specialization yields C_sum≤inf_{G,K}B(G,K); compact receiver-curve approximation, finite-grid reduction, row-stability bounds, exact Q0 coercivity, and one fixed-pair weak-duality certificate conditionally giving C_sum≤0.369296945969202842443 are available, while premise authentication, unrelaxed convergence, receiver optimality, and matching achievability remain open. In the Marton direction, the finite-auxiliary quantities are unconditionally bounded and superadditive and have a certified RTD threshold. Conditional-product architectures are additive, arbitrary two-letter candidates must pass four padding-correlation tests, and every candidate improving on twice the one-letter RTD optimum must have full support with certified mass floors. Such a candidate must now also have q_1,q_2∈(3/8,5/8), 17/20<q_1+q_2<23/20, total within-receiver output correlation below 7/160 bits, and input covariance magnitude below 7/40; the reflected/transposed family additionally requires 1/8<alpha<5/13. These are necessary conditions only. Full-support, conditionally coupled laws satisfying all constraints remain unresolved.
value.localResidualSummary: Authenticate or independently prove the external converse and achievability premises. Convert compact receiver-curve approximation and relaxed-row stability into an unrelaxed converse limit, strengthen receiver coercivity, and assess optimality of the certified fixed pair. Derive exact binary-BSSC posterior and multiletter constraints for genuine code-induced laws while retaining coupling absent from the additive relaxed UV scalars. In the achievability direction, search only among genuinely nonfactorizable full-support two-letter Marton laws satisfying the symbol-mass floors, four padding tests, marginal-balance windows, output-correlation cap, and input-covariance cap, with the additional alpha-window on the reflected/transposed family; compare candidates rigorously against 2L_RTD. Clarify finite-auxiliary cardinality scope and never infer a capacity converse from a fixed blocklength. Exact capacity still requires closing the converse gap and supplying a matching achievable rate.

placementAudit.rationale: The accepted claim is an independently reusable necessary-condition theorem that directly narrows the existing two-letter multiletter Marton search. It depends on the established Marton-to-input reduction and exact RTD threshold, belongs in the existing multiletter Marton support-search program, and changes no program hierarchy. The direct program and root summaries are updated to incorporate the new marginal, output-correlation, covariance, and one-parameter-family restrictions while preserving their necessary-only scope.
